correctness.rationale: For z(t)=t+it^2, the two deck symmetries t->i-t and t->-i-t of z and its coefficient-conjugate reflection imply that any rational quotient of polynomial pullbacks with modulus one on the parabola has period 2i, hence is constant. The squared-modulus difference of two degree<=n complex polynomials is a real polynomial in t of degree<=4n, so any 4n+1 distinct samples enforce phase-equivalence. Sharpness is all-degree: the base pair z-100i and (z-50i)/4 has two positive u=t^2 magnitude crossings; adding distant imaginary roots and scaling one branch by alpha between A_n^-1/2 and 1 creates two additional separated crossings, until exactly 2n positive simple u roots yield 4n distinct t samples. The n=0 case and Euclidean similarity reductions are addressed. Independent exact rational Sturm isolations for n=1,2,3 corroborated the inductive signs but do not replace the all-degree proof.

value.rationale: Identifies an exact worst-case deterministic sampling number for a natural curved real analytic sampling arc and gives nontrivial reflection-group phase rigidity plus an explicit matching obstruction in every degree. A generic-position result would not replace this for arbitrary predetermined sample sites.

limitations: Exact magnitude measurements only, degree<=n complex polynomials, known distinct locations, nondegenerate parabola under Euclidean similarities.
No claims on generic sample complexity, noisy stability, or arbitrary meromorphic function reconstruction.
